edges.description: Loss of the aldolase step causes accumulation of its substrate 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate and related hydroxyproline metabolites.
Accumulated 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate is proposed to be exported to the cytosol and converted to glyoxylate, which is oxidized to oxalate.
Increased endogenous oxalate raises urinary calcium oxalate supersaturation.
Calcium oxalate supersaturation leads to recurrent kidney stones.
Increased urinary HOG and related hydroxyproline-pathway metabolites report the HOGA1 metabolic block and are used diagnostically for PH3.

nodes.description: PH3 typically presents in early childhood with recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis. In contrast to PH1 and PH2, the outcome is generally favorable and progression to end-stage kidney disease is uncommon.

nodes.description: Despite a block in the mitochondrial conversion of hydroxyproline to glyoxylate, endogenous oxalate production increases in PH3. The leading proposed mechanism is that accumulated 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate is exported to the cytosol and cleaved by a non-HOGA1 cytosolic aldolase to glyoxylate, which is oxidized to oxalate; accumulated substrate may additionally inhibit glyoxylate reductase. The precise pathomechanism remains uncertain.
